paper.title_en: Modified Expansion and the JWST CMB Optical Depth Tension in Cosmology inspired by Self-Interaction Gravity
paper.abstract_en: Recent JWST observations suggests an earlier and more efficient reionization history, and thus larger Thomson optical depths than inferred from the from the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We test whether a modified expansion history motivated by self-interaction (SI) gravity can reduce this tension while retaining the standard astrophysical description of reionization. The parameters of an SI-motivated depletion function are constrained with a Bayesian MCMC using Union3 Type Ia supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, and the CMB acoustic scale $(θ_*)$. We then compute the ionization history and optical depth, including cosmology-dependent remapping of UV luminosity functions. The predicted optical depth drops from $τ_{\rm CMB}=0.0745\pm0.0001$ in $Λ$CDM to $τ_{\rm CMB} = 0.0643 \pm 0.001$ in the SI-motivated background. This shifts agreement with Planck PR3 to $\sim1.4σ$, versus $\sim3σ$ in $Λ$CDM, easing the tension. While the SI-motivated model slightly improves the best fit to the combined data, information criteria show no significant preference over $Λ$CDM.
